A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title and framework name. Their text, equations, Tables 1–12, Figures 1–9, and Appendices A–J support reliable comparison; rendered inspection resolves plot-text extraction issues.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and downstream-task experiments on six KILT datasets, alongside ablations, sensitivity analyses, model comparisons, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original KILT results and appendix experiments under the renamed framework LLM2GR.

M1.justification: LLMRefLoc is renamed LLM2GR. Section 2 retains the same Trie-constrained title generation, FM-index-constrained passage recall, weighted scoring, and short-prefix localization using KMP.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Wikipedia-based KILT coverage: NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, ELI5, FEVER, and WoW. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain Contriever, BM25, and DPR, with the same no-retrieval Llama-2-13b comparison in Table 3. Table 6 retains the same model variants, and the case studies retain BM25 comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 and the appendices retain the same validation splits, sample sizes, metrics, model configurations, decoding procedures, and experimental sweeps. Main settings remain beam sizes 15/10, k=2, prefix length 16, passage length 150, and alpha=0.9.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the same component ablations. Appendices D–J retain the same weighting, prefix-length, fine-tuning, few-shot, document-count, beam-size, and case-study analyses, with unchanged evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly report that experimental results come from a single run. Neither adds seed information, repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and case-study passages are unchanged after matching the framework rename. For example, Llama-2-13b retains NQ R-Precision 57.77 in Table 1 and TriviaQA downstream EM 72.94 in Table 3.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), their scoring definitions, and Appendix A's Trie, FM-index, and BWT explanations are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about independent constrained recall, two-stage retrieval, prefix-based acceleration, and downstream benefits. The new title and framework name do not change these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of ablations and failure cases are retained. The limitations still address competitiveness with supervised retrievers, dependence on document titles and pretraining exposure, and additional training for knowledge updates.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, document reconstruction instructions, Appendix C prompts, A100 40G hardware disclosure, timing and memory information, and repository/data references remain unchanged. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against sparse, dense, and generative retrieval remain unchanged. Generative retrieval was already discussed in v1; the new title does not introduce a revised relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Can Large Language Models Recall Reference Location Like Humans?' to 'Generative Retrieval with Large Language Models', and LLMRefLoc becomes LLM2GR throughout. Small copy edits include 'assist' to 'assists' in the abstract; section order and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The framework rename updates Figure 2's caption and result/case-study table labels, with small table-width and line-wrapping adjustments. All figures and tables retain their organization and placement, and the diagrams and plotted content are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 retitles and renames the work and makes small editorial corrections. The methods, empirical evidence, appendix analyses, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. These cosmetic adjustments do not establish a meaningful overall improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
